rules.rationale: Main-group halides are maximally ionic with closed-shell cations; no d-states in gap, giving the widest experimental gaps.
Strong ionicity and deep O 2p valence band place oxides high on the electronegativity-difference gap ladder.
Partially filled d bands introduce states near the Fermi level, narrowing or closing gaps.
Polarizable S/Se/Te p-states raise the valence band and shrink gaps; the largest anion population needs an explicit penalty.

skills.hypothesis: Ranks anion chemistry by cation-anion electronegativity difference, rewarding ionic halides and oxides while penalizing polarizable chalcogenides and d-band metals. Fails for d0 transition-metal oxides and defect-dominated experimental structures deviating from ionicity ordering.

rules.rationale: Halides had the most negative source refractive-index effect; low polarizability inverts to wide experimental band gaps via Moss.
Largest source refractive-index effect; covalent metalloid networks are classic narrow-gap semiconductors under Moss inversion.
High mean-Z boosted source refractive index; diffuse heavy-atom orbitals increase bandwidth and reduce band gap.
Independent ionicity support: deep O 2p valence band and large electronegativity difference favor wide gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Counter-hypothesis blending Moss-inverted source penalties on metalloids and heavy-Z with domain ionicity rewards, dropping the low-confidence chalcogenide inversion. Fails where high index and wide gap coexist in ionic heavy oxides, or low source confidence misleads inversion.

lesson: Development seeds gave the ionicity skill a higher mean AUC (72.7 vs 65.3) with comparable final-best, and both shared a hard seed (229102/229104) reflecting task variance rather than skill flaws. I keep ionicity chemistry as deployment, strengthen it by adding an explicit chalcogenide penalty for the largest anion population, and preserve the Moss-inverted transfer as a hybrid counter-hypothesis. Source per-field confidences remain low (0.006-0.30), so domain-grounded ordering stays the safer frozen choice.
revision_summary: Converted conditions to catalog-field-to-value maps, kept exactly two skills with four rules each. Deployed skill v2 adds a chalcogenide narrow-gap penalty (the 1485-count anion family) to the previously stronger ionicity ladder and slightly reduces its d-band and semantic mass reliance. The second skill is a hybrid counter-hypothesis retaining Moss-inverted metalloid and heavy-Z penalties but dropping the near-zero-confidence chalcogenide inversion and adding an independent oxide ionicity reward. All parameters stay within allowed ranges; no target outcomes or candidate identifiers are referenced, and feedback was used only for relative ranking, not causal mechanism claims from few seeds.
